# Hash-pinned install set for the pip bootstrap step, Python 3.9 edition.
#
# Direct requirements: pip
#
# This is the Python 3.9 counterpart of pip-bootstrap.txt, and exists for one
# reason: that file pins pip==26.2.1, which declares Requires-Python >=3.10.
# A matrix cell running 3.9 cannot install it at all, so before this file the
# only options at such a call site were an unpinned `pip install --upgrade
# pip` or a job that fails outright. Both are worse than a slightly older
# pinned pip.
#
# pip 26.0.1 is the LAST pip release that still supports Python 3.9. 26.1
# moved Requires-Python to >=3.10 and every release after it has kept it
# there, so this pin does not move again until the repo drops 3.9. (The note
# in pip-bootstrap.txt rounds this to "pip 26.x requires Python >= 3.10";
# the precise boundary is 26.1, not 26.0.)
#
# Installed with `pip install --require-hashes`, which refuses to install
# anything not listed here with a matching hash -- so the job gets the exact
# artifacts this file names, or it fails. pip has no dependencies of its own,
# so the whole closure is the one name.
#
# Each version lists the sha256 of EVERY distribution PyPI publishes for it
# (the pure-Python wheel, plus the sdist). pip accepts a download that matches
# any one of them, so the pin does not quietly depend on the runner resolving
# to the same artifact this file was generated against -- which is what lets
# one file serve an ubuntu/macos/windows matrix.
#
# Updating: Dependabot owns the routine bumps (see the /.github/requirements
# pip entry in .github/dependabot.yml) and rewrites the hashes with them.
# Expect it to propose 26.1+ here; that bump must be REFUSED while any 3.9
# cell still installs this file, because it reintroduces exactly the
# Requires-Python failure this file exists to avoid.
#
# That refusal is enforced, not remembered: tests/test_pip_bootstrap_py39_pin.py
# fails any pin at 26.1 or above, and runs in ci.yml's Syntax & Lint job on
# every PR. It has to be checked there, because the only job that installs this
# file -- release-canary.yml -- does not run on pull requests, so a bump to a
# pip that cannot install on 3.9 is green on every PR check and breaks the
# release path after it merges. Dependabot has proposed exactly that (#6047).
# The guard's boundary is "below 26.1", not "exactly 26.0.1", so a 26.0.x
# release is still free to land here.
#
# What staying on 26.0.1 accepts: pip 26.0.1 is named by four published
# advisories -- GHSA-58qw-9mgm-455v, GHSA-jp4c-xjxw-mgf9, GHSA-qwm4-qh6w-59xr
# and GHSA-wf93-45jw-7689 -- all fixed in releases that require 3.10+, so no
# fix is reachable from here. This is a deliberate acceptance, and the exposure
# it carries is narrow: every one of those advisories concerns what pip does
# while RESOLVING and fetching from an index, and the two installs this pip
# performs are this file itself (--require-hashes, one name, exact artifact
# already verified) and a `clawmetry==<version>` from PyPI in the canary job.
# It is CI-only -- no released wheel, no user machine, and one call site. The
# acceptance ends when the repository drops Python 3.9: at that point delete
# this file, point the canary's matrix at pip-bootstrap.txt, and drop the guard.
#
# Regenerating by hand:
#   pip install --dry-run --ignore-installed --report r.json 'pip==26.0.1'
# then, for each resolved name==version, take every sha256 under `urls` in
# https://pypi.org/pypi/<name>/<version>/json.

pip==26.2 \
    --hash=sha256:bdb1b08f4274833d62c1aa29e20907365a2ceb950410df15fc9521bad440122b \
    --hash=sha256:c4037d8a277c89b320abe636d59f91e6d0922d08a05b60e85e53b296613346d8
